card: This PR updates CheckTxInputs unit tests to support multiple inputs and adds test cases where inputs cumulatively exceed MAX_MONEY or contain negative values. Previously, unit tests only exercised single-input transactions, leaving a mutation that weakens the consensus money range validation condition undetected. The change is confined to unit tests in transaction_tests.cpp.
changed_since_previous: Added an additional test case covering a transaction containing a negative input value ({2 * COIN, -1 * COIN}).
evidence: PR description notes that current unit tests leave mutant 275 alive in `Consensus::CheckTxInputs` (changing `if (!MoneyRange(coin.out.nValue) || !MoneyRange(nValueIn))` to `&&`): 'the current checktxinputs_invalid_transactions_test only covers cases with one input, so the sum nValueIn is always equal to coin.out.nValue'.
problem: Existing unit tests in `transaction_tests.cpp` for `Consensus::CheckTxInputs` only tested transactions with a single input. Because `coin.out.nValue` always equaled `nValueIn`, test coverage missed cases where `nValueIn` independently exceeds range limits or where negative input values appear alongside valid ones, allowing mutation tests (such as changing `||` to `&&` in the money range check) to pass undetected.

risk.why: Only modifies unit tests in transaction_tests.cpp without touching production consensus code.

summary: Extends the `checktxinputs_invalid_transactions_test` helper in `transaction_tests.cpp` to support transactions with multiple inputs. Adds test cases where individually valid input values exceed `MAX_MONEY` when summed, and where an input value is negative. This ensures that `Consensus::CheckTxInputs` rejects transactions whose cumulative or individual input values violate consensus money range rules.
